question.text: What is the role of the 'Designated Director' in the context of PMLA compliance?

answer.text: A person designated by the reporting entity to ensure overall compliance with obligations under Chapter IV of the PMLA and the Rules made thereunder
A government official appointed by the Central Government to oversee all PMLA investigations
The CEO of a reporting entity who is personally liable for all financial transactions processed
An external auditor hired to conduct annual reviews of a reporting entity's financial statements

explanation.text: The Logic: The Designated Director is a person designated by the reporting entity to ensure overall compliance with the obligations imposed under Chapter IV of the PMLA and the Rules made thereunder. The role sits alongside the Principal Officer in the reporting entity's AML governance, and FINGate registration includes the Designated Director who is responsible for the AML programme. The Trap: Option B is the government-official distractor — the Designated Director is internal to the reporting entity, not appointed by the Central Government. Options C and D incorrectly equate the role with the CEO or with an external auditor. Note: Both the Principal Officer and the Designated Director are registered with FIU-IND via the FINGate portal, so candidates must distinguish the two internal compliance roles.
